content:
# Deuteronomy 30 — Disagreement Log
**SOPHIA** | EMET vs. LOGOS vs. PNEUMA | 20 verses ("choose life" chapter)

---

## V.1 — "Call them to heart" vs. "take them to heart"

- **EMET:** "and you take [them] to heart [vahasheivota el-levavecha] among all the nations"
- **LOGOS:** "and you call them to heart among all the nations"
- **PNEUMA:** "and you take them to heart wherever the LORD your God has scattered you"

**Differences:** EMET and PNEUMA: "take them to heart"; LOGOS: "call them to heart" — an unusual English idiom. PNEUMA also changes "where the LORD your God has driven you" to "wherever... has scattered you" (importing the language of v.3). **Resolution:** "take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you" — EMET/PNEUMA for the idiom; EMET for the exact relative clause.

---

## V.1 — "Driven you" vs. "scattered you"

- **EMET:** "where the LORD your God has driven you"
- **LOGOS:** "where the LORD your God has driven you"
- **PNEUMA:** "wherever the LORD your God has scattered you"

**Differences:** PNEUMA: "scattered you" in v.1 — but the Hebrew hedeichakha ("has driven/banished you") is distinct from the verb "scatter" (pitz/puz) used in v.3 (hiphatsekha). EMET/LOGOS preserve the distinction. **Resolution:** "where the LORD your God has driven you" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.2 — "Sons" vs. "children"

- **EMET:** "you and your sons"
- **LOGOS:** "you and your children"
- **PNEUMA:** "you and your children"

**Differences:** EMET: "sons" (baneicha — the literal Hebrew); LOGOS/PNEUMA: "children." In the context of covenant restoration, baneicha encompasses all descendants broadly. **Resolution:** "you and your children" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; contextually appropriate.

---

## V.2 — "Listen to his voice" vs. "obey his voice" vs. "obey him"

- **EMET:** "listen to his voice"
- **LOGOS:** "obey his voice"
- **PNEUMA:** "obey him"

**Differences:** EMET: "listen to his voice" — the more literal rendering of ve-shama'ta be-qolo; LOGOS: "obey his voice" — captures the covenantal force; PNEUMA: "obey him" — drops "his voice" entirely. The Hebrew qol (voice) is significant in Deuteronomy as the vehicle of covenant instruction. **Resolution:** "obey his voice" — LOGOS; retains "voice" and captures covenantal force.

---

## V.3 — "He will return and gather you" vs. "he will gather you again"

- **EMET:** "he will return and gather you from all the peoples"
- **LOGOS:** "he will gather you again from all the peoples"
- **PNEUMA:** "gather you again from all the nations"

**Differences:** EMET: "he will return and gather you" — the Hebrew ve-shav ve-qibetzkha uses shuv again (the chapter's keyword of return). LOGOS/PNEUMA: "gather you again" — smooths the Hebrew idiom but loses the resonance of shuv appearing in three consecutive verses (vv.2, 3, 8). **Resolution:** "he will gather you again" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; more idiomatic. The shuv resonance is noted but does not justify awkward English.

---

## V.3 — "Peoples" vs. "nations"

- **EMET:** "all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you"
- **LOGOS:** "all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you"
- **PNEUMA:** "all the nations where he scattered you"

**Differences:** EMET/LOGOS: "peoples" (ha-ammim); PNEUMA: "nations" and drops the subject "the LORD your God." The Hebrew ha-ammim is specifically "peoples," distinct from goyim (nations) used in v.1. PNEUMA also drops the divine name. **Resolution:** "all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.4 — "Ends of the heavens" vs. "uttermost parts of heaven" vs. "most distant land"

- **EMET:** "at the ends of the heavens"
- **LOGOS:** "in the uttermost parts of heaven"
- **PNEUMA:** "to the most distant land under the heavens"

**Differences:** EMET: "ends of the heavens" — literal qetsot ha-shamayim (the far ends/horizon); LOGOS: "uttermost parts of heaven" — archaic but accurate; PNEUMA: "most distant land under the heavens" — paraphrase that adds "land" not present in the Hebrew. **Resolution:** "at the ends of the heavens" — EMET; literal and vivid.

---

## V.4 — "Bring you back" plus in PNEUMA

- **EMET:** "from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will take you"
- **LOGOS:** "from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will take you"
- **PNEUMA:** "from there the LORD your God will gather you and bring you back"

**Differences:** PNEUMA: "bring you back" for the Hebrew ve-laqach otekha ("and will take you") — adds "back" which is interpretive. EMET/LOGOS: "take you" — literal. **Resolution:** "from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will take you" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.5 — "Do you good and multiply you" vs. "make you more prosperous and numerous"

- **EMET:** "he will do you good and multiply you more than your fathers"
- **LOGOS:** "he will make you more prosperous and numerous than your fathers"
- **PNEUMA:** "He will make you more prosperous and numerous than your ancestors"

**Differences:** EMET: "do you good" (ve-heitivkha) and "multiply you" (ve-hirbkha) — literal; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "more prosperous and numerous" — combines both verbs interpretively. PNEUMA: "ancestors" for avoteicha. **Resolution:** "make you more prosperous and numerous than your fathers" — LOGOS; idiomatically clear. "Ancestors" is a needless departure from avoteicha.

---

## V.6 — "Your heart and the heart of your offspring" vs. "your hearts and the hearts of your descendants"

- **EMET:** "your heart and the heart of your offspring"
- **LOGOS:** "your heart and the heart of your offspring"
- **PNEUMA:** "your hearts and the hearts of your descendants"

**Differences:** PNEUMA: pluralizes "hearts" — not matching the Hebrew singular levavekha ("your heart"). EMET/LOGOS: singular "your heart" is literal and theologically pointed (each individual heart is circumcised). **Resolution:** "your heart and the heart of your offspring" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.6 — "So that you will love" vs. "to love"

- **EMET:** "to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your being [nephesh]"
- **LOGOS:** "so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul"
- **PNEUMA:** "so that you may love him with all your heart and with all your soul"

**Differences:** EMET: "to love... with all your being [nephesh]" — the infinitive and Hebrew gloss; LOGOS: "so that you will love... with all your soul"; PNEUMA: "so that you may love him" — drops the divine name. **Resolution:** "so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul" — LOGOS; "nephesh" as "soul" in this context is the established rendering.

---

## V.7 — "Enemies and those who hate you" vs. "foes and enemies"

- **EMET:** "your enemies and upon those who hate you and who persecuted you"
- **LOGOS:** "your foes and enemies who persecuted you"
- **PNEUMA:** "your enemies who hate and persecute you"

**Differences:** EMET: preserves two distinct categories — oyeveicha (your enemies) and sone'eicha (those who hate you); LOGOS: conflates into "foes and enemies"; PNEUMA: preserves "enemies who hate you" but drops the second noun. The Hebrew has both terms as separate objects. **Resolution:** "your enemies and upon those who hate you and who persecuted you" — EMET; both terms are preserved.

---

## V.8 — "Return and listen" vs. "again obey"

- **EMET:** "And you shall return and listen to the voice of the LORD and do all his commandments"
- **LOGOS:** "And you shall again obey the voice of the LORD and keep all his commandments"
- **PNEUMA:** "You will again obey the LORD and follow all his commands"

**Differences:** EMET: "return and listen" — the Hebrew ve-attah tashuv ve-shamata — two verbs: return (shuv) + listen/obey (shama'); LOGOS: "again obey" — combines them; PNEUMA: drops "voice of the LORD" and changes "keep" to "follow." **Resolution:** "And you shall again obey the voice of the LORD your God and keep all his commandments" — LOGOS with "the LORD your God" restored.

---

## V.9 — "Make you abound" vs. "make you abundantly prosperous" vs. "make you most prosperous"

- **EMET:** "will make you abound in all the work of your hand"
- **LOGOS:** "will make you abundantly prosperous in all the work of your hand"
- **PNEUMA:** "will make you most prosperous in all the work of your hands"

**Differences:** EMET: "abound" — closer to the Hebrew Hiphil of yathar/ra'vah; LOGOS: "abundantly prosperous"; PNEUMA: "most prosperous" (superlative not in the Hebrew). PNEUMA also pluralizes "hands." **Resolution:** "will make you abundantly prosperous in all the work of your hand" — LOGOS.

---

## V.9 — "Rejoice over you for good" vs. "take delight in prospering you" vs. "delight in you and make you prosperous"

- **EMET:** "the LORD will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers"
- **LOGOS:** "the LORD will again take delight in prospering you, as he took delight in your fathers"
- **PNEUMA:** "The LORD will again delight in you and make you prosperous, just as he delighted in your ancestors"

**Differences:** EMET: "rejoice over you for good" — Hebrew ve-sas... le-hativkha; LOGOS: "take delight in prospering you" — captures both the rejoicing and the prospering; PNEUMA: "just as he delighted in your ancestors" (ancestors vs. fathers). **Resolution:** "the LORD will again take delight in prospering you, as he took delight in your fathers" — LOGOS.

---

## V.10 — "Scroll of the Torah" vs. "Book of the Instruction"

- **EMET:** "this scroll of the Torah"
- **LOGOS:** "this Book of the Instruction"
- **PNEUMA:** "this Book of the Instruction"

**Differences:** EMET: "scroll of the Torah" — sefer ha-Torah literally rendered; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "Book of the Instruction" — following the project convention for Torah in deuteronomic contexts. **Resolution:** "this Book of the Instruction" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; project convention.

---

## V.11 — "Not too difficult" vs. "not too hard" vs. "not too difficult or beyond your reach"

- **EMET:** "not too difficult for you [lo nifle'at hi mimcha]"
- **LOGOS:** "not too hard for you"
- **PNEUMA:** "not too difficult for you or beyond your reach"

**Differences:** EMET: "not too difficult" with Hebrew gloss; LOGOS: "not too hard"; PNEUMA: adds "or beyond your reach" — importing language from the spatial metaphors of vv.12–13 (not in the Hebrew of v.11). **Resolution:** "not too difficult for you" — EMET; clean, accurate, without over-reading.

---

## V.12 — "Go up for us to the heavens" vs. "ascend to heaven for us"

- **EMET:** "Who will go up for us to the heavens and take it for us and cause us to hear it"
- **LOGOS:** "Who will ascend to heaven for us and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Who will ascend into heaven to get it and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?"

**Differences:** EMET: "go up for us to the heavens" — more literal of the Hebrew mi ya'aleh lanu ha-shamayimah; LOGOS: "ascend to heaven for us" — cleaner English; PNEUMA: "proclaim it to us" for ve-yashmi'enu otah ("cause us to hear it"). The Hebrew is "cause us to hear," not "proclaim." **Resolution:** "Who will ascend to heaven for us and bring it to us and cause us to hear it, that we may do it?" — LOGOS for "ascend" but EMET/LOGOS for "cause us to hear."

---

## V.13 — "Beyond the sea" vs. "across the sea"

- **EMET:** "And it is not beyond the sea... Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea"
- **LOGOS:** "Neither is it beyond the sea... Who will cross to the beyond the sea for us" [sic]
- **PNEUMA:** "Nor is it beyond the sea... Who will cross the sea to get it"

**Differences:** EMET: "cross over for us to the other side of the sea" — the Hebrew mi ya'avor lanu el-ever ha-yam; LOGOS has a grammatical error ("cross to the beyond the sea"). PNEUMA: "cross the sea to get it" — drops "the other side." **Resolution:** "Who will cross the sea for us to the other side and bring it to us and cause us to hear it, that we may do it?" — EMET's structure, with LOGOS's "bring it to us" for consistency with v.12.

---

## V.14 — "So that you can do it" vs. "to do it"

- **EMET:** "in your mouth and in your heart — to do it"
- **LOGOS:** "It is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it"
- **PNEUMA:** "it is in your mouth and in your heart so you may obey it"

**Differences:** EMET: "to do it" — the Hebrew infinitive la'asoto; LOGOS: "so that you can do it"; PNEUMA: "so you may obey it." EMET is most literal. LOGOS adds the modal "can." PNEUMA substitutes "obey" for "do." **Resolution:** "in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it" — LOGOS; the modal adds appropriate nuance.

---

## V.15 — "Life and good, and death and evil" vs. "life and prosperity, death and destruction"

- **EMET:** "life and good, and death and evil"
- **LOGOS:** "life and good, death and evil"
- **PNEUMA:** "life and prosperity, death and destruction"

**Differences:** EMET/LOGOS: "good" (tov) and "evil" (ra') — the fundamental moral poles of Deuteronomy; PNEUMA: "prosperity" and "destruction" — an interpretive rendering importing the chapter's economic/agricultural imagery. Tov and ra' are not merely material categories here; they carry full moral weight. **Resolution:** "life and good, and death and evil" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.16 — Conditional structure vs. causal structure

- **EMET:** "in that I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God..." (causal/relative)
- **LOGOS:** "If you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, by loving..." (conditional)
- **PNEUMA:** "For I command you today to love the LORD your God..." (explanatory)

**Differences:** EMET follows the Hebrew asher (relative/causal particle) closely; LOGOS restructures as a conditional sentence; PNEUMA uses "For." The Hebrew syntax in v.16 flows from v.15 as an exposition of what "life and good" means. EMET's structure preserves the grammatical connection. **Resolution:** "in that I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his rules" — EMET.

---

## V.16 — "Ordinances" vs. "rules"

- **EMET:** "his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances"
- **LOGOS:** "his commandments and his statutes and his rules"
- **PNEUMA:** "his commands, decrees, and laws"

**Differences:** The Hebrew mitsvotav, chuqqotav, u-mishpatav — "commandments, statutes, and rules/ordinances." EMET: "ordinances"; LOGOS: "rules"; PNEUMA: "laws." The established rendering of mishpatim in Deuteronomy for this project is "rules" (following LOGOS). **Resolution:** "commandments and his statutes and his rules" — LOGOS.

---

## V.17 — "Turns away" — additional clause

- **EMET:** "But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to other gods and serve them"
- **LOGOS:** "But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but are drawn away to worship other gods and serve them"
- **PNEUMA:** "But if your heart turns away and you are not obedient, and if you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and worship them"

**Differences:** (1) "Do not listen" (EMET) vs. "will not hear" (LOGOS) vs. "are not obedient" (PNEUMA) for ve-lo tishma. (2) "Bow down and serve" (EMET/PNEUMA) vs. "worship and serve" (LOGOS) for ve-hishtachavita va-avadtam. The Hebrew hishtachavah specifically means "to bow down/prostrate," a physical act. **Resolution:** "But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them" — EMET.

---

## V.18 — "Surely perish" vs. "certainly be destroyed"

- **EMET:** "you shall surely perish"
- **LOGOS:** "you shall surely perish"
- **PNEUMA:** "you will certainly be destroyed"

**Differences:** EMET/LOGOS: "surely perish" — the Hebrew avod tovadun (infinitive absolute: "perishing you shall perish"); PNEUMA: "certainly be destroyed" — adds passivizing and stronger destructive connotation. **Resolution:** "you shall surely perish" — EMET/LOGOS.

---

## V.18 — "Yarden" vs. "Jordan"

- **EMET:** "crossing the Yarden to enter and possess"
- **LOGOS:** "going over the Jordan to enter and possess"
- **PNEUMA:** "crossing the Jordan to enter and possess"

**Differences:** EMET: "Yarden" — the Hebrew name; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "Jordan." Project convention: English name forms in consensus translation. **Resolution:** "crossing the Jordan to enter and possess" — LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## V.19 — "Call to witness against you" — word order

- **EMET:** "I call to witness against you today the heavens and the earth: life and death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse"
- **LOGOS:** "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse"
- **PNEUMA:** "This day I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses"

**Differences:** (1) EMET's word order: witnesses first, then the content ("life and death I have set..."); LOGOS/PNEUMA: "I have set before you" placed after witnesses. (2) EMET/LOGOS: "blessing and curse" (with or without articles); PNEUMA: "blessings and curses" (pluralized — not in the Hebrew). (3) PNEUMA: "This day" — inverts the Hebrew ha-yom. **Resolution:** "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse" — LOGOS with EMET's definite articles restored.

---

## V.19 — "Choose life" — leading conjunctions and additions

- **EMET:** "and you shall choose life [u-vacharta ba-chayyim], so that you may live, you and your offspring"
- **LOGOS:** "Therefore choose life, that you and your offspring may live"
- **PNEUMA:** "Now choose life, so that you and your children may live"

**Differences:** EMET: "and you shall choose life" — the vav-consecutive with the bare perfect/imperative; LOGOS adds "Therefore"; PNEUMA adds "Now." Both "Therefore" and "Now" are interpretive additions not in the Hebrew u-vacharta. PNEUMA: "children" for zar'akha ("your offspring/seed"). **Resolution:** "choose life, so that you and your offspring may live" — bare imperative without added conjunctions; "offspring" over "children" for zar'a.

---

## V.20 — Infinitive vs. participial construction

- **EMET:** "to love the LORD your God, to listen to his voice, and to cling to him"
- **LOGOS:** "loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice and holding fast to him"
- **PNEUMA:** "that you may love the LORD your God, listen to his voice, and hold fast to him"

**Differences:** EMET: infinitive constructs (le-ahavah, lishmoa', lidbaqah); LOGOS: present participles; PNEUMA: purpose clause ("that you may..."). The Hebrew infinitives flow as the content of "choosing life." LOGOS's participials give the ongoing-relational sense. **Resolution:** "loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him" — LOGOS; the participial construction captures the sustained character of the covenant life.

---

## V.20 — "Cling" vs. "hold fast"

- **EMET:** "to cling to him" (lidbaqah)
- **LOGOS:** "holding fast to him"
- **PNEUMA:** "hold fast to him"

**Differences:** EMET: "cling" — the Hebrew daqab means to cling/cleave (used also in Gen 2:24 of a man cleaving to his wife). LOGOS/PNEUMA: "hold fast" — more idiomatic. Both capture the relational intensity. **Resolution:** "holding fast to him" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; idiomatic and established in formal English Bible tradition.

---

## V.20 — "He is your life and the length of your days" vs. "he will give you many years"

- **EMET:** "for he is your life and the length of your days"
- **LOGOS:** "for he is your life and length of days"
- **PNEUMA:** "For the LORD is your life, and he will give you many years"

**Differences:** EMET/LOGOS: "he is your life and the length of your days" — ki hu chayyekha ve-orekh yameicha; PNEUMA: "he will give you many years" — paraphrases ve-orekh yameicha ("the length of your days") as a future promise rather than a present identification. EMET/LOGOS preserve the theological force of the LORD being identified as the substance of life and longevity. LOGOS drops the article in "length of days." **Resolution:** "for he is your life and the length of your days" — EMET.

---

## V.20 — "To your fathers" vs. "to your ancestors"

- **EMET:** "to your fathers — to Avraham, to Yitschak, and to Ya'akov"
- **LOGOS:** "to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob"
- **PNEUMA:** "to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob"

**Differences:** EMET: "fathers" with Hebrew name forms; LOGOS: "fathers" with English names; PNEUMA: "ancestors" with English names and without the repeated "to." The Hebrew la-avotekha — "to your fathers." Project convention: "fathers" and English name forms. **Resolution:** "to your fathers — to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob" — LOGOS name forms with EMET's repeated "to" structure preserved.

---

*Total disagreements logged: 41*
*Arbiter: SOPHIA*
